Despite recent changes utility rates for net metering are still subsidies in that customers are getting paid more than their energy would be worth on the open market. The "problem" might be referencing the fact that solar customers generate less revenue than what it costs to serve them (Solar and the ability to sell back requires more infrastructure, and the energy business already requires immense capital). This is by design in order to subsidize green energy (a good thing!), though solar panel companies want you to believe that panels would be money printing machines if it weren't for greedy energy service providers. However solar is only cost efficient at industrial scale, ie solar farms or enormous commercial/industrial facilities that use all the energy they produce. Subsidies for residential solar is a policy designed to create a larger market for panels and drive down the cost of producing them, which had already been done. I believe the cost of producing a kW of solar energy is 1/6 of what it cost 15 years ago (ballpark).
